quiz_item.question: When cutting, tooling, and dyeing vegetable-tanned leather for Leatherwork Requirement 1, which workshop safety practices are required?
options: A. Hold the leather strip in the palm of your hand while slicing toward your thumb with a utility knife, and use solvent leather dyes in a closed bedroom.

B. Cut leather on a firm cutting mat or poly board with a sharp knife held securely and always slice away from your non-cutting hand and body; use a poly or rawhide mallet (never a steel hammer) on stamping tools over a marble or granite slab; and apply solvent-based dyes and contact cements only with adequate ventilation and gloves.
C. Strike hardened steel leather stamps with a heavy carpenter's claw hammer to send metal shards flying across the table.
D. Test the sharpness of a swivel knife or skiver blade by drawing it across the pad of your index finger.
